summary: XRD analysis in this paper demonstrates the coexistence of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals and a Cs4PbBr6 crystalline matrix within a hybrid material. The XRD pattern shows peaks attributable to both phases, supporting the structural model of perovskite nanocrystals embedded in a hexabromide host. Additional characterization (SEM, TEM, SAED, ICP-AES) corroborates this phase coexistence and the proposed composite structure.

key_findings.finding: XRD spectra show peaks corresponding to both CsPbBr3 and Cs4PbBr6, confirming the coexistence of these two phases in the hybrid material.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The hybrid material consists of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals embedded within a Cs4PbBr6 matrix, as evidenced by the simultaneous presence of both phases in the XRD pattern.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The XRD pattern displays peaks assigned to both CsPbBr3 and Cs4PbBr6, and the caption and text explicitly state the coexistence of these phases. This supports the model of nanocrystals within a matrix.

citations.evidence: XRD spectra of a CsPbBr 3 -in-Cs 4 PbBr 6 crystal.
Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Figure 3b ) confirms the coexistence of perovskite and hexabromide compounds in the material system.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The XRD data alone confirm phase coexistence but do not provide quantitative phase fractions or crystallite size information.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: While the presence of both phases is clear from the XRD peaks, there is no quantitative analysis (e.g., Rietveld refinement, peak area ratios, or Scherrer analysis) reported in the supplied data.

limitations.claim: No full width at half maximum (FWHM) or quantitative peak width data are provided, limiting the ability to estimate crystallite size or strain from the XRD data.
Only one XRD figure is present, so trends with respect to experimental variables (e.g., composition, processing conditions) cannot be established.
Quantitative phase fractions are not determined from the XRD data; the ratio of CsPbBr3 to Cs4PbBr6 is instead estimated from ICP-AES, not XRD.

citations.evidence: Processed ICP-AES data showing the ratio of the compounds.
